data.long_meaning: One who seeks refuge, healing or forgiveness. The name Ruqee carries the meaning “Seeker of healing or forgiveness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ruqee usually hope their child will grow to embody seeker of healing or forgiveness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ruqee carries significant cultural importance in the Islamic world as it is associated with the concept of seeking refuge or protection from Allah (swt). This can take various forms such as seeking forgiveness for past mistakes, protection from harm, or seeking strength during times of trial. The name is often used as a term of endearment for those who are moments of need. It's also a reminder of the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and seeking His help and guidance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ruqee holds deep spiritual significance for Muslims as it reminds us of the importance of seeking Allah's refuge and protection in this life and in the hereafter. It is a reflection of the belief that Allah is the only source of true healing, peace, and forgiveness. The name also serves as a reminder to constantly turn to Allah in all aspects of life, seeking His guidance and strength. Ultimately, the name Ruqee embodies the Islamic principles of turn to Allah, seek His forgiveness, and trust in His mercy and protection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Seeker of healing or forgiveness" symbolizes One who seeks refuge, healing or forgiveness. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ruqee serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of seeker of healing or forgiveness.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyya, Zad Al-Ma'ad, Volume 2, Page 596 The name Ruqee carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mention of Ruqyah (healing through recitation of Quran) and Ruqi (healer) in the context of seeking relief from physical and spiritual harm.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Rushd (Averroes), Al-Kulliyyat Al-Tibbiyyah (The Comprehensive Book on Medicine), Section on 'Mental Disorders', Page 571
historical_references.context: Discussion on therapeutic use of Ruqyah (recitation of Quran) in the treatment of mental disorders and its efficacy in calming the mind.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ruqyah' or 'Ruqee' in Islamic tradition refers to the act of seeking spiritual healing through recitation of the Quran, supplications, and the use of holy water. In today's world, Ruqyah is gaining popularity as a form of spiritual self-care and mental health support. On Instagram, users can find numerous accounts dedicated to sharing Ruqyah practices, tips, and resources. TikTok is filled with short clips showcasing Ruqyah practices, often accompanied by calming music and soothing visuals. Finally, on YouTube, there are tutorials and explanations of Ruqyah practices, as well as live sessions for spiritual healing. The modern context of Ruqyah emphasizes its role in promoting overall wellbeing, reducing stress, and improving mental health.
